skeleton:
Mini Full English Brunch Plates

British · Easy · Makes 4 mini plates

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The full English in miniature: every component scaled to a single exquisite bite or two — a quail's egg, a cocktail sausage, half a rasher, a medallion of black pudding, a hash brown coin, a cherry tomato, one mushroom — plated as its own small breakfast for a brunch table of grazers. The mini plate is the full English as canapé, and it is more than a novelty: the small format forces precision, cooks faster than the full plate, and lets a table of six eat the whole canon in one sitting. The technique is the same architecture at one-third scale, with quail eggs as the one genuine new skill — they poach in 90 seconds and fry in 45, and their yolks are proportionally richer. Everything else is knife-work: small, uniform, and honest.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The mini components (per plate, ×4)

  • or 1 large egg for the "one egg" version
  • from the homemade master's mix, or cut from a frozen one

Seasoning and fat

- **Uniform smallness is the plate's law:** everything cut to the same two-bite scale — a cocktail sausage's length, a 4 cm medallion, a halved cherry tomato. One oversized component breaks the plate's honesty. - **The quail eggs at room temperature** and cracked into a small cup each — their shells are stubborn and the yolks are brave; cracking against a flat surface, not an edge, avoids shell shards in the cup. - One tray plus one pan: the tray takes the roasting components at 200 °C, the pan takes the fried ones. The whole plate cooks in 20 minutes of parallel work.

Mini Full English Brunch Plates

Prep: 20 minutes · Cook: 25 minutes · Total: 45 minutes · Makes 4 mini plates

Ingredients

The mini components (per plate, ×4)

  • 3 cocktail sausages or 1 standard sausage cut in thirds (40 g per plate)
  • ½ rasher back bacon (25 g), cut in half crosswise
  • 1 slice black pudding (25 g), cut with a 4 cm pastry ring into a medallion
  • 3 quail eggs (45 g) — or 1 large egg for the "one egg" version
  • 1 small hash brown coin (40 g) — from the homemade master's mix, or cut from a frozen one
  • 2 cherry tomatoes (60 g), halved
  • 50 g button mushrooms, whole if tiny
  • 1 slice (30 g) baguette or a small square of fried bread

Seasoning and fat

  • 15 ml / 14 g neutral oil
  • 15 g butter
  • 2 g fine sea salt
  • 1 g black pepper
  • 1 tsp (2 g) brown sugar, for the tomatoes
  • Brown breakfast sauce and tomato ketchup, in espresso spoons

Instructions

  1. **The tray — sausages, hash coins, tomatoes, mushrooms — 15 minutes at 200 °C.** Everything oiled, salted, and spread small-side-by-side: cocktail sausages (pricked once), hash brown coins, cherry tomato halves cut-face up with a sugar grain each, and the button mushrooms. Roast 12–15 minutes, turning the sausages and coins once. Checkpoint — sausages browned and taut; coins deep gold both faces; tomatoes slumped to jammy half-moons; mushrooms browned and shrunk to intense little buttons. Everything at its own correct doneness — the tray's small scale makes synchrony easy.
  2. **The bacon and black pudding medallions — 6 minutes in the pan.** While the tray runs, cook the bacon pieces pressed flat to glassy, and the black pudding medallions 2 minutes a side to crusted. Checkpoint — bacon flat and amber at cocktail scale (it crisps faster — watch it); medallions crusted, holding, miniature.
  3. **The quail eggs, 90 seconds.** Butter in the pan over medium heat; when it foams, slide in the quail eggs. Fry 45–60 seconds undisturbed — the whites set astonishingly fast — and lift with a small spatula while the yolks still dome. Checkpoint — whites set, yolks domed and trembling, proportionally huge — the mini plate's crown jewels and its best bite.
  4. **Plate the minis — four small plates, one composition each.** Baguette slice toasted and buttered at the centre; the components arranged around it in the full English's geography, miniaturised: egg at the crown, bacon and sausage flanking, medallion and coin at the sides, tomato and mushroom filling. Sauce in its espresso spoon beside. Checkpoint — each plate reads as a complete full English at arm's length — the full architecture in miniature — and every component is eaten in one or two bites, yolk broken over the coin at the first move.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Quail yolks set solidHeat high or eggs lingeredMedium butter, 45–60 seconds, lift while doubtful
Components cooked unevenlyMixed scales on one trayThe uniform-smallness law; coins and sausages turned together
Medallions crumbledCut thin or cold cutter4 cm ring, 1 cm thick, straight press
Plates looked sparseBread skippedThe toasted centre slice is the plate's anchor — it is not optional

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- **Components batch and reheat** (3 days, 180 °C for 6 minutes); the eggs are always à la minute — the whole point of the plate. A brunch for eight is 40 minutes of cooking and a fine hour. - **Variation — the brunch board:** all the minis on one shared board rather than plated — the grazing version, and the host's easiest morning. - **Variation — the luxury minis:** quail eggs, quail sausages (chipolatas), and a shaving of black truffle over the medallions — the full English at its most country-house. - **The scale lesson:** cooking the canon small teaches the canon's timing better than any single big plate — every component's doneness is visible at a glance, and the whole architecture fits in one pan's glance.

If the first one's yolk firms, the pan was a notch hot for the rest; adjust and continue. It is the butter-basted master's patience, compressed by nine grams.
